newsitem.title: USA: CompuServe would consider any sale offers.
newsitem.headline: CompuServe would consider any sale offers.

text.p: CompuServe Corp Chairman Frank Salizzoni on Friday said its board of directors would consider selling the company if any offers emerged.

"If there is somebody out there that is interested, then obviously we have to consider strategic alternatives like that," Salizzoni told reporters after the company's uneventful annual meeting. He is also acting chief executive officer.
CompuServe's corporate services unit has performed well, but its consumer online service has struggled.
Overall, the company lost $1.10 a share in the first three quarters of its fiscal year, which ends April 30, compared with earnings of $0.68 in the year-earlier period.
Salizzoni said it would not make sense to create two separate companies because both utilize CompuServe's network. He said the infrastructure was one of the company's strengths.
H&R Block Inc still plans to spin off its remaining CompuServe interest, possibly before CompuServe returns to profitability, said Salizzoni, who is also Block's president and chief executive.
Block postponed the spin-off in August. Block owns 80 percent of CompuServe after spinning off a one-fifth stake in an April 1996 initial public offering.
"We wanted to stabilize the financial situation, get the trends moving in the right direction (and) increase the cash position, which we're doing," he said.
CompuServe's fiscal third-quarter loss of $0.15 a share was narrower than its second-quarter loss of $0.63, and the company showed a positive operational cash flow.
Salizzoni declined to forecast when CompuServe might return to profitability.
Salizzoni said he had interviewed one candidate for the chief executive post, vacated last month by Robert Massey. He declined to say when someone might be chosen for the job.
He repeated the online provider's view that a lawsuit filed against it this week by Time Warner Inc's Time magazine was without merit.
